core_obligations: Set up the comparison of truncations (proof lines 6922-6938): the commutative diagram for epsilon gives Rf_{tau',*} R epsilon_{X,*} F = R epsilon_{Y,*} Rf_{tau,*} F, hypothesis (V_n) says that the map from epsilon_{X,*} F to its derived version is an isomorphism in degrees at most n, and hence the same holds after applying Rf_{tau',*}.

Run the induction on the spectral sequence (proof lines 6962-6988): with (C_m) the assertion in degrees at most m, (C_0) is immediate, and for m < n the author shows that all terms E_2^{p,q} with p > 0 and q <= m-1 vanish by the induction hypothesis and (V_n); hence E_2^{0,m} is the only term with p + q = m, no differentials touch it, and (C_m) follows.

Settle the top degree (proof lines 6990-7017): for (C_{n-1}) the same analysis leaves only the differential emanating from E_2^{0,n}, producing a short exact sequence; since both outer sheaves satisfy the sheaf property for tau-coverings while the tau-sheafification of the third is zero by the companion results on locality of cohomology, the first map in that sequence is an isomorphism, which is the statement.
proof_roadmap: Use the commutative diagram of epsilon to move the comparison to the level of derived pushforwards and truncate using (V_n).
Analyse the second page of the relative Leray spectral sequence and prove the graded comparison by induction on the degree.
Treat the final degree, where the only obstruction is a single differential, and remove it with the sheaf property and the vanishing of higher direct images.
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that under the comparison situation, hypothesis (V_n) implies R^i f_{tau',*} epsilon_{X,*} F = epsilon_{Y,*} R^i f_{tau,*} F for i at most n (statement lines 6913-6919). The proof is a substantial spectral sequence induction: after turning the commutative diagram of the morphism epsilon into a comparison of derived pushforwards and truncating it by (V_n) (proof lines 6922-6938), the author displays the second page of the relative Leray spectral sequence (proof lines 6938-6961) and proves the graded statements (C_m) by induction, showing that the terms with p > 0 and small q vanish (proof lines 6962-6988); the top degree needs a separate argument in which the only surviving differential gives a short exact sequence whose first map is forced to be an isomorphism by the sheaf property and the vanishing of the higher direct images (proof lines 6990-7017). The non-formal content is the two-page bookkeeping and the top-degree argument. The claim is H2: a structured induction with every input named.
